Hi Elena —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call today. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned on performance requirements and what we’ll validate in the POC:

Summary of SLOs you called out:
- P95 generation latency: <= 120ms (target) for single-turn chat responses (~50 tokens)
- First-byte streaming latency: <= 200ms for streaming use cases
- Sustained throughput: 150 reqs/s for peak (with occasional spikes to 300 reqs/s)
- Concurrency: ~200 concurrent sessions during peak windows
- Availability: 99.9% (we’ll surface Dedicated options for contractual SLAs)

Open questions we flagged:
1) Are you comfortable with a model variant that’s quantized (4-bit) if it reduces cost but may change quality slightly?
2) Do you have strict tail-latency requirements for >1k token responses, or is the focus on short/medium responses?
3) Which endpoints will use streaming vs non-streaming (we need this to size batching/latency behavior)?

Next steps (action items):
- I’ll share a short SLO worksheet (attached) for you to confirm targets across dimensions.
- Priyom (SE) and Rishi (SRE) will propose cost/perf levers (batching, caching, quantization profiles, model variants) and an initial infra sizing for the POC.

Subject: RE: Performance SLO follow-up & cost/perf levers — NovaRetail

Thanks Elena — I’ve reviewed the filled worksheet. A couple of quick notes and an initial proposal for levers we should test during the POC:

Key clarifying points:
- For streaming-first UX, we’ll validate both first-byte and incremental token latency. First-byte ~= server-side model compute + network; our target is <200ms on typical West Coast locations.
- For spike behavior, we’ll test burst capacity via autoscale + temporary routing to lower-cost model variants if Dedicated pool is saturated.

Initial cost/perf lever recommendations (to evaluate in POC):
1) Continuous batching (dynamic micro-batching): preserves low latency at low QPS while increasing throughput. Useful for predictable traffic — should reduce unit cost by ~20-35% depending on request size.
2) Prefix/KV caching (per-account and shared caches): with high cache hit rates for repeated prompts we can avoid repeated attention compute. Expect 10-40% cost reduction on conversational workloads with good reuse.
3) Quantization profiles (8-bit/4-bit + mixed precision): start with 8-bit for minimal quality impact, pilot 4-bit variants for non-critical paths. We’ll run side-by-side A/B evals on your sample prompts to detect regressions.
4) Model variant routing: use a higher-accuracy unquantized variant for validation/critical flows and a quantized smaller variant (e.g., redwood-v3-7b-4bit) for cost-sensitive, non-critical flows.
5) Streaming vs batch route separation: prioritize streaming requests onto low-latency nodes with smaller batching windows; batch long-response jobs onto throughput-optimized nodes.

Deliverables before POC kickoff:
- Rishi will provide an initial infra sizing (GPU type / instance counts) for peak and sustained loads.
- I’ll prepare an A/B prompt evaluation plan comparing full-precision and quantized variants on your sample prompts.
- Marissa will coordinate kickoff date and success criteria.

Cheers,

Quick sizing note based on the worksheet numbers (150 reqs/s sustained, 200 concurrent, p95 120ms):

- Suggested baseline: Dedicated pool using A100-class (or equivalent) GPUs, with mixed-instance sizing for burst (2x rtx-a6000-like nodes + 6x a100-like high-throughput nodes).
- Concurrency model: allocate warm worker threads to maintain low p95; enable continuous batching with a max batch window tuned to keep p95 under 120ms for 50-token responses.
- Caching: enable per-account prefix caching (TTL 5m for session reuse); expect 15-30% effective token savings on conv flows.
- Quantization plan: start with 8-bit for POC (fast to validate). If A/B shows <2% metric delta on your eval set, we can roll 4-bit for high-volume non-critical routes.
- Fallbacks: configure routing policies to fallback to higher-capacity nodes or a less-quantized variant if model latency degrades.

I’ll attach a short sizing spreadsheet and a sample runtime config after this message (won’t attach binary here). If you want absolute cost estimates I can run a cost model once we lock the exact token profile and live traffic shape.
